strings.name: Carol Greider
strings.summary: Carol Greider detected telomere-extending enzyme activity as a doctoral student in Elizabeth Blackburn's laboratory and later studied telomerase RNA and its mechanism. At Cold Spring Harbor, Johns Hopkins and the University of California, she investigated links among telomere length, cell proliferation and disease. She shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Blackburn and Jack Szostak, demonstrating the lasting value of curiosity-driven research.

strings.influence.rationale: Co-discovered telomerase and advanced research on chromosome-end protection, cellular aging and mechanisms related to disease.

strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: UC Santa Barbara biology bachelor's (1983); UC Berkeley molecular-biology PhD (1987)
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Co-discovered telomerase
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Detected telomere-extension activity with Blackburn in Tetrahymena and validated it through further experiments.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Telomere length and cell fate
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Studied telomerase RNA, telomere shortening and proliferation, providing foundations for research on disease mechanisms.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Joined UC Santa Cruz
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Accepted a distinguished professorship and moved her telomere-biology research to UCSC.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Shared Nobel medicine prize
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Honored with Blackburn and Szostak for discoveries about chromosome-end protection.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Shared Lasker Award
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Recognized with Blackburn and Szostak for basic research on telomeres and telomerase.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Moved to Johns Hopkins
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Joined the medical school to continue telomerase biochemistry and telomere-dysfunction research.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Telomeres shortened during division
strings.timeline.event-5.text: With colleagues reported shortening of telomeres as cultured human cells divided, informing studies of proliferation limits.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Doctorate and Cold Spring Harbor
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Completed her Berkeley PhD and continued independent telomerase research at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Detected telomere-extension activity
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Observed repeated DNA-extension signals in Blackburn's laboratory, then tested alternatives and validated a new enzyme.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Biology bachelor's degree
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Graduated from UC Santa Barbara before doctoral study at Berkeley.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Born in San Diego
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Born in San Diego, California, and later grew up in Davis.
